text:
**For a lot of cells at once, a 16-bay charger is the best fit.** My search results don't include direct purchase links for any of them, so the links below go to the review pages that cover each one.

## 16-bay options
- **Tenergy TN438 (16 bays):** This is the one I'd look at first. It takes any mix of AA and AAA NiMH/NiCd cells in any slot. It has an LCD showing each cell's status, protection against overcharge, overheating, short-circuit and reverse polarity, and an 8-hour timer. ([source](https://electronicsadvisor.org/best-nimh-battery-charger/))
- **BONAI 16-Bay:** Slots are independent and you can mix AA and AAA. It runs on 110-240V AC at 250-500 mA per port, with LEDs for charging, full and faulty cells. It won't charge alkaline or lithium cells. ([source](https://electronicsadvisor.org/best-aa-battery-chargers/))
- **POWEROWL 16-Bay:** It has 16 independent channels and a four-stage charge process (pre-charge, quick, float, trickle). ([source](https://electronicsadvisor.org/best-aa-battery-chargers/))
- **CITYORK 16-Bay:** It has a smart LCD and a vented design for heat. ([source](https://electronicsadvisor.org/best-nimh-battery-charger/))

## If 8 bays is enough
**Tenergy TN480U, $23.99.** It charges 8 AA or AAA cells mixed, at 500 mA per AA and 250 mA per AAA. It has a per-slot LCD and bad-cell detection. It takes USB-C or Micro-USB input, and the adapter isn't included. Use a 2 A source, because on a 1 A source five or more AA cells drop to 250 mA each. The source doesn't confirm that each bay is fully independent. [Buy the TN480U](https://dealectric.com/go/tenergy-tn480u-8-bay-nimh-charger). This is an affiliate link, so Dealectric is paid if you buy, at no cost to you. ([source](https://dealectric.com/answers/best-high-capacity-aa-aaa-nimh-battery-charger-8-bay-16-bay-independent-channels))

Other 8-bay choices are the EBL 8-Bay, which has per-slot LEDs and safety shutoff, and the NICEBATT Smart 8-Bay, which has USB-C input. ([source](https://electronicsadvisor.org/best-aa-aaa-charger/))

## Things to know
- All of these are NiMH/NiCd only. Never put alkaline or lithium cells in them.
- Dealectric says it has no 16-bay charger on record. That's a limit of their catalog, not of the market.
- The Electronics Advisor pages are affiliate-driven roundups, and I haven't seen independent lab testing. Check recent buyer reviews on the specific listing before you buy.
- If you also need cells, the Tenergy Premium PRO 2,800 mAh AA 20-pack is $42.99. ([buy](https://dealectric.com/go/tenergy-premium-pro-aa-2800mah-20-pack), also an affiliate link)

I'd go with the TN438 if you want 16 bays, or the TN480U if 8 is enough.
